data.title: Choose the correct answer for each question.
data.description: Practise basic adjective position and simple adjective order in common A1 noun phrases.
data.learningTitle: Putting Adjectives in the Right Place
learningPoints: Put most adjectives before the noun they describe.
Do not normally put an adjective after a noun in a basic noun phrase.
Use adjectives after forms of the verb 'to be'.
When two simple adjectives come before a noun, opinion commonly comes before size.
Do not add -s to an adjective when the noun is plural.

sections.summary: Putting an adjective before a noun.
sections.explain: In a basic noun phrase, the adjective normally comes before the noun.

words.word: She has a red car.
She has a car red.
She has a reds car.

sections.explain: An adjective can come after AM, IS or ARE.

words.word: The house is big.
The house big is.
The is house big.

sections.summary: Keeping adjectives unchanged with plural nouns.
sections.explain: English adjectives do not normally take a plural -s.

words.word: They are small dogs.
They are smalls dogs.
They are dogs small.

sections.explain: In simple adjective order, size normally comes before colour.

words.word: He has a big black bag.
He has a black big bag.
He has a bag big black.

sections.explain: A simple opinion adjective normally comes before a size adjective.

words.word: It is a nice small café.
It is a small nice café.
It is a café nice small.

sections.explain: A colour adjective normally comes directly before the noun if it is the only adjective.

words.word: She is wearing a blue dress.
She is wearing a dress blue.
She is wearing a blues dress.

sections.explain: Size normally comes before colour in a simple two-adjective phrase.

words.word: We have a small white table.
We have a white small table.
We have a table small white.

sections.explain: After LOOKS meaning 'appears', use an adjective.

words.word: Your room looks clean.
Your room clean looks.
Your clean looks room.

sections.summary: Putting an age adjective before a noun.
sections.explain: An age adjective such as OLD or NEW normally comes before the noun.

words.word: They live in an old house.
They live in a house old.
They live in an olds house.

sections.explain: In simple adjective order, size generally comes before age.

words.word: He bought a small new phone.
He bought a new small phone.
He bought a phone small new.
